sections.heading: What Wichita Homeowners Call Us About
body: Most breakdowns come down to one part, and the symptom usually points to it. Here is what we look for, and what we do about it.

items.title: The house won't get below 80
items.text: The vents blow warm. A weak capacitor, a worn fan motor or a refrigerant leak is usually the cause, and we fix that part.

items.title: The outdoor unit hums and the fan never spins
items.text: A weak capacitor can't give the motor its starting jolt. It's one of the cheapest and most common AC repairs, and we replace it once we've confirmed it's the cause.

items.title: The AC shuts off and water sits by the unit
items.text: Algae has usually clogged the condensate drain, and a safety switch has tripped to protect the house. We clear the line and check why it clogged.

items.title: The furnace clicks but never lights
items.text: A dirty flame sensor or a worn igniter is the usual reason. We test both, tell you which one failed, and replace only that.

items.title: It runs all afternoon and the house still sits at 82
items.text: On an older system that has needed repeated repairs, each fix buys a few months. We lay the repair next to replacement, with reasons for each, and you decide.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace
body: A new system is the biggest bill in this trade, so it should never be the first thing you hear. If a capacitor, a motor or an igniter has failed on a system that otherwise runs well, repair it.
Replacement starts to make sense when the system is old, the repairs keep coming, or it's on the older R-22 refrigerant. The label on the outdoor unit shows the age and refrigerant.
When it is time, we install new air conditioners and furnaces. Here is [what a replacement involves](/ac-replacement-wichita-ks/).

sections.heading: Warm Air, Silent Unit: What Usually Fails
body: The thermostat says 74, the house says 85, and the vents blow warm. Heat is when an air conditioner works hardest, so heat is when parts quit. Most of the time it's one failed part, not a dead system.
Here is what we usually find, and what we do about it.
tail: We'd rather find the real cause and fix it once than guess and have to come back.

items.title: The unit hums but the fan won't start
items.text: A weak capacitor, the small part that gives the motors their starting jolt. We replace it, and it is one of the cheapest and most common fixes.

items.title: The fan or compressor stalls
items.text: Hours of Kansas heat wear a motor's bearings and windings. We confirm the motor is the cause, then replace it.

items.title: Cool air that isn't cold
items.text: A system doesn't use up refrigerant, so low levels mean a leak. We find the leak instead of just topping off.

items.title: The system shuts off and water sits by the unit
items.text: Algae has clogged the condensate drain and a safety switch tripped. We clear the line and check why it clogged.

items.title: Ice on the coil
items.text: Restricted airflow, usually a dirty filter, lets the coil freeze over. Turn the system off to thaw it, and we find why the air was restricted.

items.title: The AC won't turn on at all
items.text: A tripped breaker is the first thing to rule out, and a failed contactor or a dead control board is next. We test each one, tell you which one failed, and replace only that.

sections.quote: My AC motor stopped working and they were able to make it out within an hour of calling and get my unit fixed. The communication, service and price were great! 10/10 recommend.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace?
body: Repair when the system is fairly young and one part has failed. A new capacitor or motor on a system that otherwise runs well is money well spent.

Replace when most of these are true: the system is 10 to 15 years old or more, it has broken down repeatedly, it runs on the older R-22 refrigerant, or it can't keep the house cool even with every part working.
We give you the reasoning and the numbers on both, and you choose. If it does come to replacement, here is [what a new system involves](/ac-replacement-wichita-ks/).
Annual tune-ups are part of what we offer, so a weak part gets caught on a mild day instead of failing on the hottest one.

sections.heading: Not Sure It's the AC?
body: A quick check can save you a visit:
list: Confirm the thermostat is set to cool, below the room temperature, with working batteries.
Check that the breaker for the outdoor unit and the indoor air handler hasn't tripped.
Look at your air filter. If it's packed with dust, replace it.
Check for ice on the refrigerant lines or the indoor coil. If you see ice, turn the system off and let it thaw before calling.
tail: If those don't fix it, call and tell us what you see and hear. That helps us arrive with the right parts.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Call
body: Tell us how old the system is and what it's doing, and we book you the same day or the next. Emergency calls are available, summer included.

The technician finds what failed and explains your options in plain words: repair the part, replace a major component, or replace the system. You get the reasoning and the numbers on each, and you decide.

sections.heading: Repair First, When Repair Makes Sense
body: Replacement is not where we start. A young system with one failed part should be repaired, and we'll tell you so. If your system has years left, you'll hear that from us.

sections.heading: When the System Is Telling You It's Done
body: You've paid for the same system three summers running. It runs all afternoon and the house still sits at 82. The outdoor unit rattles, the vents are weak, or the electric bill climbs while the comfort drops.
None of those alone means replace. Together they usually do. Each repair buys a few months, not years.

Most central air conditioners are built to last around 10 to 15 years, and Kansas summers sit at the hard end of that range. As a system ages, repair calls come closer together and it uses more electricity to deliver less cooling.
A system on the older R-22 refrigerant is also getting costly to service, because that refrigerant is no longer produced. A new system fixes all three at once.

sections.heading: What We Install
body: We install energy-efficient air conditioning systems for homes, matched to your house and your needs. The goal is a system that is the right size for your home, not the biggest one on the truck.
Size matters. A system that's too large cools fast, shuts off and leaves the house clammy. One that's too small runs nonstop and can't keep up on a 100-degree day.
If part of your space has no ductwork, ask us about a ductless mini split.
Same-day and next-day appointments are available, and the estimate is free.
